comments.body:
## Status 2026-10-27 ~22:15 PDT — not implemented this session; one new fact that changes the hypothesis set

The operator decision recorded on this ticket (land only the trace-preservation change plus a failure message that distinguishes "git chose not to run maintenance" from "maintenance ran but was not a descendant") is the right scope and I did not change it. **No code was written for this ticket in this session.**

One finding from the sibling store bugs is directly relevant to candidate mechanism 2, and should be on the record before the next reproduction attempt.

### The host's git behaviour in a tracker-sized repo is load-dependent in a way the fixture does not control

Measured today on this host, in the real tickets tracker (213,713 index entries, 34.7 MB index):

- `git status --porcelain` took **49 s**, because every index entry was stat-dirty and git had to re-hash all 213 k files.
- `git diff-files --name-only` (stat-only, no re-hash) over the same index took **6 s**.
- rebar's own store seam bounds git at **30 s** (`sync._GIT_TIMEOUT`), and the synthetic `"git timed out after 30s"` outcome was independently observed on this host for a `git commit` at ~18:40 PDT.

The bd66 detector asserts that git ran auto-maintenance *as a descendant of a commit*. Git's decision to start `--auto` maintenance, and whether that work completes far enough to emit a traced process, is sensitive to how long the surrounding commit takes and to object-DB state — both of which move by an order of magnitude under full-suite load on this host. That does not identify the mechanism, and it is **not** evidence for any of the three candidates. It does say that "the structural assertion is not timing-dependent, but the CONDITION it detects is" (already in the description) is sharper than it looks: the condition depends on git's own cost-based heuristics, which this host's load visibly perturbs.

### Recommendation unchanged, with one addition

Land the trace-preservation change and the discriminating failure message as decided, and when the next natural failure yields a Trace2 file, record alongside it: the commit's wall-clock duration, `gc.log` presence, and `git count-objects -v` at failure time. Without the commit duration the captured trace still cannot separate "git declined maintenance" from "maintenance was cut short", which is candidate mechanism 2.

Reproduction attempts remain at **4, zero reproductions** — unchanged from the earlier comment. Nothing here rules any candidate in or out.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## Second independent reproduction, with the bound identified

Reproduced on 2026-10-31 during a full `make verify` for story `8257-3a28-e757-4079`, worktree `impl-8257` at `9424881459c`, `PYTEST_WORKERS=4`, macOS/arm64:

```
FAILED tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py::test_the_trace_check_detects_maintenance_inside_a_commit
1 failed, 20134 passed, 27 skipped, 48 warnings in 7570.96s (2:06:10)
```

The failure is a timeout, not an assertion:

```
rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar create failed (exit 1):
Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s
src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:166: RebarError
```

It raises inside `_create_two_tickets_traced` at `:186`, before the test reaches any of its assertions.

### The bound, and why this test is the one that hits it

`src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py:38` sets `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 30`. That bounds every git call in the commit path.

In production that bound is comfortable, because `gitutil.py:328` defines

```python
_AUTOMAINT_OFF: tuple[str, ...] = ("-c", "gc.auto=0", "-c", "maintenance.auto=false")
```

and `event_append.py:434,:488` pass it to every `git commit`, so `git maintenance run --auto` and its repack can never run inside a commit at all.

This test deliberately removes that protection:

```python
tracker = _cross_the_maintenance_threshold(repo)
monkeypatch.setattr(event_commit_git, "_AUTOMAINT_OFF", ())
```

So it first creates enough loose objects to *guarantee* a repack fires, then strips the suppression so the repack really does run inside the commit — all under the same 30s bound. **The test's design maximizes the cost of the operation it then wall-clock-bounds.** That makes it load-sensitive by construction, which is consistent with this ticket's title: the test added to fix a flake is itself the flake.

### Isolation measurement

Same tree, same host, test run alone (while 2 other `make verify` runs continued):

```
1 passed in 52.62s
```

**The test body takes 52.62s against a 30s per-git-call bound.** The margin is not large even when the test is otherwise alone, and the repack is a single call inside that 52s. Under 4-way xdist plus concurrent verifies, one git call crossing 30s is unsurprising.

### Scope check — the change under test cannot be implicated

`8257`'s diff is 23 files, every one under `docs/adr/`:

```
23 files changed, 958 insertions(+), 27 deletions(-)
git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep -v '^docs/'   ->   (no output)
```

No source file, no test file, nothing in the store path. The change cannot affect git commit maintenance behavior, which is why I treated the failure as this ticket's rather than the story's.

### Note on the predecessor

`99fb-a2f3-3e9d-4116` (closed) raised the bound from 1s after the same class of failure in `test_write_survives_foreground_maintenance_repack`. The 30s figure inherited that fix. Raising it again would be the third iteration of the same move, so the durable fix is more likely to be bounding what the test asks git to do — capping the loose-object fill, or asserting on the trace without requiring the repack to complete within the commit's own timeout — than another increase.

## Third reproduction — and the diagnosis message from 3135 cannot fire on this failure path

Reproduced again on 2026-11-01 during a full `make verify` for story `c670-c285-a0f9-4b40`,
worktree `impl-c670` at `938e962c5d8`, `PYTEST_WORKERS=4`, macOS/arm64, worker `gw2`:

```
FAILED tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py::test_the_trace_check_detects_maintenance_inside_a_commit
1 failed, 20140 passed, 27 skipped in 4265.25s (1:11:05)
```

`c670`'s diff is `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `docs/adr/*`, `evals/similar-tickets/*`, and
`tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py` — nothing under `src/rebar/_store/`. Isolated on
that same tree the test passes: `1 passed in 31.38s`. Three other `make verify` runs were in
flight on the host at the time (`impl-25a4`, `impl-f5f5`, `impl-8257`); 1-minute load average 36.

### The finding: this failure mode bypasses `_maintenance_diagnosis` entirely

The 2026-10-27 operator decision left this open so that "the next natural failure's log will
identify which of the three candidate mechanisms" applies, relying on the enriched detector
message merged as Gerrit 3135. That cannot happen, because the enriched message is unreachable
on the path that actually fails.

`_maintenance_diagnosis(trace, tracker)` appears exactly once, in the message of the final
assertion of `test_the_trace_check_detects_maintenance_inside_a_commit`:

```python
assert any("maintenance" in o for o in offenders), (
    "removing the suppression produced no maintenance descendant of a commit: "
    f"{offenders}\n{_maintenance_diagnosis(trace, tracker)}"
)
```

Reaching that line requires `_create_two_tickets_traced` to **return**. The observed failure
raises *inside* it, at `test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py:186` — the first of its two
`rebar.create_ticket` calls:

```
src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:166: RebarError
E   rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar create failed (exit 1):
    Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s
```

So the trace is never parsed, `offenders` is never computed, and the diagnosis never runs. Every
occurrence of this flake under load will take the same path, because the timeout is what fails.
Waiting for another natural failure will keep producing this same evidence-free traceback.

### What this implies for the fix

The two failure modes are distinct and only one is instrumented:

- **"git chose not to run maintenance"** — `_create_two_tickets_traced` returns, `offenders` is
  empty, the assert fails, and 3135's diagnosis correctly names the mechanism. Not what is
  happening here.
- **"the commit exceeded its bound"** — `create_ticket` raises before any assertion. This is the
  observed mode in all three reproductions, and it carries no mechanism evidence.

The test deliberately maximizes the cost of the operation it then bounds: `_cross_the_maintenance
_threshold` guarantees a repack will fire, and `monkeypatch.setattr(event_commit_git,
"_AUTOMAINT_OFF", ())` removes the suppression that keeps production from ever paying that cost
inside a commit (`event_append.py:434,:488`). The body therefore runs a full repack inside a
commit bounded at `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 30` (`event_commit_git.py:38`). At 31s solo, the margin is
under 1 second, so any concurrent load pushes it over.

Raising the bound a third time (predecessor `99fb-a2f3-3e9d-4116` already took it from 1s to
30s) would restore green without addressing that the test's own body exceeds the bound it runs
under. If the diagnosis evidence is still wanted, it needs to be captured on the timeout path —
not only on the assertion path.

## Correction to the comment above: two distinct failure modes, not three of one

The previous comment said the timeout "is the observed mode in all three reproductions". That is
wrong about the original. Re-reading this ticket's own description, the 2026-10-26 failure was the
**assertion** mode:

> The failing assertion is the detector's:
> `assert any("maintenance" in o for o in offenders)`
> so `commits >= 1` held — commits WERE traced — but with `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` emptied, git ran no
> maintenance/gc/repack/pack-objects/multi-pack-index process as a descendant of a `git commit`.

So the record is 3 failures across **2 distinct modes**:

| Date | Story / worktree | Mode | Reaches `_maintenance_diagnosis`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-26 | `b6e723ceb59` | assertion — `offenders` empty, commits traced | yes |
| 2026-10-31 | `8257` / `impl-8257` @ `9424881459c` | `RebarError`: git timed out after 30s | no |
| 2026-11-01 | `c670` / `impl-c670` @ `938e962c5d8` | `RebarError`: git timed out after 30s | no |

That changes what the open decision buys rather than invalidating it. Gerrit 3135's diagnosis is
correctly aimed at the mode that produced this ticket, and it would still fire if that mode recurs.
What the two newer failures show is that the **more frequent** mode on this host — 2 of 3, both
within the last 48 hours — raises inside `_create_two_tickets_traced` at
`test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py:186` and so collects no evidence at all.

The three candidate mechanisms in the description remain neither ruled in nor out: none of them is
tested by a timeout, because the timeout aborts before git's maintenance decision can be observed.
Reproduction attempts for the **assertion** mode stay at 4 attempts, 0 reproductions.

Whether the two modes share a root cause is unestablished. They are consistent with one — a commit
that runs long enough under load either exceeds the 30s bound or gets its maintenance work cut
short, which is candidate mechanism 2 — but nothing here measures that, and the timeout path
captures neither the commit duration nor the trace that would distinguish it.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation
During a full `make verify` on this macOS/arm64 host (2026-10-26, `PYTEST_WORKERS=4`, worktree at `b6e723ceb59` plus an unrelated eval-config diff), the run ended:

```
FAILED tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py::test_the_trace_check_detects_maintenance_inside_a_commit
1 failed, 19819 passed, 88 skipped, 48 warnings in 3407.75s (0:56:47)
```

The failing assertion is the detector's:

```python
assert any("maintenance" in o for o in offenders), (
    f"removing the suppression produced no maintenance descendant of a commit: {offenders}"
)
```

so `commits >= 1` held — commits WERE traced — but with `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` emptied, git ran no `maintenance`/`gc`/`repack`/`pack-objects`/`multi-pack-index` process as a descendant of a `git commit`.

Re-run of the same file in isolation on the same tree, immediately after: `2 passed in 132.65s`.

## Why this matters
This test is **itself the fix for a previous flake**. Bug `simious-comic-marmot` (`99fb-a2f3-3e9d-4116`, closed `flaky`, landed as Gerrit change 3109 / `ae02e364465` on 2026-10-25) removed a load-sensitive 1.0 s wall-clock bound from the sibling test `test_write_survives_foreground_maintenance_repack` and replaced it with a Trace2 structural assertion. `test_the_trace_check_detects_maintenance_inside_a_commit` was ADDED by that same change, to supply "the proof the 1 s bound used to give."

So the detector written to make the invariant load-independent has now itself failed under full-suite load. The structural assertion is not timing-dependent, but the CONDITION it detects is: it requires git to actually decide to run auto-maintenance during the commit.

## What is established, and what is not
Established:
- The failure is in the detector's positive assertion, not the invariant test — the production invariant (no maintenance inside a bounded commit) was not violated.
- It did not reproduce in isolation on the same tree.
- The fixture's precondition held by construction: `_cross_the_maintenance_threshold` asserts `maintenance.autoDetach == "false"` and `count-objects >= 6700` before the creates, and the test got past both.

NOT established — the root cause. The failing run's Trace2 file lived under that run's `tmp_path` and is gone, so the actual process tree from the failure was never captured. Candidate mechanisms, none yet distinguished:
1. Git declined auto-maintenance for a reason unrelated to the loose-object count (for example a `gc.log` written by a failed/skipped gc, which suppresses further auto-gc for `gc.logExpiry`).
2. Under 4-way xdist plus ~19.8k tests, the repack that `--auto` would start was skipped or failed in a way that emitted no traced process.
3. Trace2 event-file write/read interleaving under load, so the maintenance `start` event was not yet visible when `_maintenance_inside_commits` parsed the file.

Hypothesis 3 is the one the current test shape cannot rule out: `_create_two_tickets_traced` parses the trace immediately after the second create returns, with no flush/settle barrier.

## Proposed approach (not yet decided — needs the reproduction first)
Do NOT weaken or delete the detector; its job is to keep the invariant test honest. Instead:
1. Reproduce under load with the trace PRESERVED — run the file with `-n 4` against a loaded host, and on failure copy the Trace2 file and `gc.log` out of `tmp_path` before teardown (a `tmp_path_factory` artifact dir, or an autouse fixture that copies on failure).
2. From the captured trace, determine which of the three mechanisms above holds: whether a maintenance process started at all, whether it was a descendant, and whether `gc.log` exists in the tracker.
3. Fix the cause that the evidence names. If it is (3), the fix is a settle/flush barrier before parsing, not a retry. If it is (1), the fixture must clear or assert-absent `gc.log`. If it is (2), the detector needs a precondition assert that distinguishes "git chose not to run maintenance" from "maintenance ran but was not a descendant" — today both produce the same empty `offenders` and the same opaque message.
4. Regardless of cause, improve the failure message: it currently prints `offenders` (empty) and cannot distinguish those two cases, which is why this report cannot name the mechanism.

## Scope
In scope: `tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py`, and a test-artifact-preservation helper if one is needed to capture the trace. Out of scope: production code, the `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` suppression, `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, and the explicit maintenance step — the production invariant is not implicated by this failure.

## Testing
`pytest tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py -q` and under load `-n 4`, repeated; then `make verify`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The failure is reproduced at least once with the Trace2 file and `gc.log` preserved, and the ticket records which of the three candidate mechanisms the trace shows.
- [ ] The detector distinguishes, in its failure message, "no maintenance process started at all" from "a maintenance process started but was not a descendant of a commit".
- [ ] The identified cause is fixed at the class level, with no wall-clock bound and no retry/rerun of the assertion.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py -q -n 4` passes on 10 consecutive runs on a loaded host.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.
